transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve lost all interest in my jewelry work and the things I used to love, and I can’t make myself care enough to keep the shop going. A long-time client and my husband both got really concerned about how much I've pulled away and suggested I talk to a doctor. I just feel so weary and don't know what else to do.
Have you experienced these feelings of low mood and loss of interest for the first time recently, or have you struggled with these symptoms on and off for several years?

These feelings are actually quite recent, starting about two years ago when my husband's health began to decline. It's not something I've struggled with on and off for years; instead, it has been a constant, heavy weight for a little over a year now.
Have you ever experienced a similar period in your life, even years ago, where you felt this same level of persistent sadness or loss of interest for several weeks or more?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before my husband got sick. I’ve always been a very active, hands-on person, so feeling this level of sadness and numbness is completely new to me.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns, appetite, or energy levels since these feelings began?

Yes, my appetite is completely gone and my clothes are hanging off me from losing so much weight. I also lie awake for hours with my mind racing, only to wake up around 4 AM unable to get back to sleep. Because of that, I feel completely drained of energy, like I've run a marathon even on days when I barely do anything.

Do you feel that your movements and speech have become noticeably slower or more sluggish to the point where others might have commented on it, or do you feel a sense of internal agitation and restlessness?

My body feels incredibly slow and sluggish, almost like I'm trying to move through molasses. Even simple things like getting up from the couch or reaching for my jewelry tools take so much effort that my husband has asked if I'm in physical pain. I don't feel any restlessness or agitation inside; it's just this heavy, physical slowing down.
Have these feelings of being 'slowed down' and your loss of interest become so severe that you are unable to carry out even basic daily tasks like personal hygiene or eating?

Yes, they've severely impacted my daily life, and basic things like chores and bills are piling up because everything feels too overwhelming. My body feels like it is moving through molasses, making even simple movements incredibly effortful. I've also completely lost my appetite and barely pick at my meals, which has caused my clothes to start hanging off me.
Have you experienced any persistent thoughts about life not being worth living, or have you had any thoughts of harming yourself during this difficult time?

It's hard to admit, but I have had those thoughts. Sometimes I feel like it would be a relief if I just didn't wake up, or if I took the leftover pain pills in the bathroom so my husband could find someone more capable. I've even gone as far as counting how many pills are in the bottle, though I haven't actually done anything.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being controlled by others, or have you heard voices or seen things that others around you cannot perceive?

I don't feel like my thoughts are being controlled, but I do hear a male and a female voice whispering late at night when the house is quiet, telling me I'm a terrible wife and failing. I also struggle with this persistent belief that some of my customers are secretly judging me and trying to push my shop out of business, even though there's no proof of it.
